blocks.text: Elgin Chantrell, South Surrey: Neighbourhood Guide
Living in Elgin Chantrell, South Surrey

parts.t: Elgin Chantrell is the MLS® sub-area on the south bank of the Nicomekl River in South Surrey. A small settler community was farming here by 1879, and Crescent Road still follows the river along the route first cut in 1883. Lots run from acreage zoning to suburban streets, with farmland behind the dykes, so the floodplain, the ALR line and heritage status are worth checking lot by lot.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations and school catchments before you buy or sell.

It is an MLS® sub-area on the south side of the Nicomekl River in South Surrey. Elgin is an official BC community name, and Chantrell Creek flows north into the Nicomekl. The real estate board sets the sub-area lines, so check where a listing is placed.
Where does the name Elgin come from?

W.C. McDougall chose it for the post office in 1885 after consulting neighbours, including Harry Chantrell, whose name is on Chantrell Creek. BC Geographical Names records two explanations: Lord Elgin, a governor general of Canada, or Elgin in Bruce County, Ontario. The Elgin Post Office opened on 1 November 1885.
Is Elgin Chantrell in the ALR?

Some of it is. Farmland in the Nicomekl lowland is in the Agricultural Land Reserve, and Elgin Heritage Park’s own parcel is partly ALR. ALR status is set parcel by parcel, so check the exact address on the

Is Elgin Chantrell in a floodplain?
Some low land near the Nicomekl River is. Nico-Wynd/Crescent Road is named in Surrey’s coastal floodplain, and the river is controlled by sea dams off Elgin Road, so check the exact property.
